summary: A wood-frame station of 1906 on Point Elliott, still flashing its 1852 Fresnel lens beside the Whidbey ferry landing and run as a museum by the Mukilteo Historical Society.

access.note: Grounds open year round; lighthouse and gift shop open Saturdays and Sundays 1-4 pm, April to September (Historical Society).

notes_for_editor: Thin on primary sources: the Lighthouse Board annual reports of 1903-1907 are not in the local corpus, so construction facts rest on the 2008 NRHP form (which quotes the Treasury letter of 1902 and 1906 newspapers second-hand) and HistoryLink/LighthouseFriends. Source disagreements shown in the story and left unresolved: tower height (38 ft NRHP / 30 ft HistoryLink and USLHS); fog trumpet maker (Daboll per NRHP, HistoryLink, LighthouseFriends; Cunningham per Historical Society timeline); where the present 1852 lens came from (NRHP: brought in 1927; HistoryLink: swapped with New Dungeness); Christiansen's entry to the service (1893 NRHP/HistoryLink vs 1894 assistant at Turn Point per Historical Society and TPLPS); the donated acre (1954 NRHP/HistoryLink vs 1973 LighthouseFriends); the Coast Guard's lens plan (1960 vs 'the 1960s'); Corrie's tour (NRHP to 1960, USLHS to 1958). Vivian R. Corrie appears in the archive roster as first assistant 1933-37 and principal keeper 1946-58 under one person slug (archive's own link). Brooks: NRHP says from New Dungeness; TPLPS has an E. A. Brooks at Turn Point 1898-1902 who later became Mukilteo keeper; both used. The 1914 Bulletin entry (volume p.135, PDF p.39) is cited without the month of the issue. Newspaper search (Chronicling America, WA, 1905-07 and 1925-26) found only two small San Juan Islander items. 1977 NRHP text claims the guest-register date; roster lines for USCG personnel carry no rank or position. The Dec 1933 Bulletin text is column-interleaved OCR, so quotes there are short fragments. A site position check: the record's OSM position (47.9487, -122.3064) matches LighthouseFriends; the USLHS position (47.9319, -122.305) is about 1.9 km south and looks wrong (minute-level rounding). Light List characteristic 'Fl W 5s' from the record; NRHP agrees (2 s flash every 5 s). The 'climbable' flag follows the NRHP and the Historical Society's tours, subject to the seasonal hours. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the NRHP summary gives 35 feet for the lighthouse height (Section 8 says 38); the story now says so. The 1925 Bulletin item gives the rescue date (4 September), not its own date.
